history.summary: IDENTITY: Generic name flagged. Documented with the best-supported referent: the Laxmi Narayan temple in Kailashahar town, Unakoti district, Tripura. A Tripura government Unakoti District newsletter states that in 1964 the Laxmi Narayan temple at Kailashahar was established by the Sevayet (caretaker) Krishnananda and was constructed with financial assistance from the Tripura royal family; a Tamal tree was planted in front of the temple about 60 years ago in honour of Lord Krishna's association with the Tamal tree in the Bhagavata legend, and the temple celebrates Janmashtami and Durga Puja annually. A travel vlog describes Laxminarayan Bari Mandir as located in Kailashahar town, 3-4 km from Unakoti. CSV town 'Kailashahar' is CORRECT for this row; CSV state 'Tripura' is correct. District corrected to Unakoti (the CSV carries no district column; Kailashahar is the Unakoti district HQ). town_description: Kailashahar is the headquarters of Unakoti district in Tripura, a historic town on the Manu river surrounded by the Unakoti hills, about 178 km from Agartala by road. It is a diverse, predominantly Hindu (90%) town hosting temples including the Lakshmi Narayan temple, the 14 Deities Temple of Rangauti, a New Kali temple and a Sringeri Sharada Peetham, alongside mosques and churches. Unakoti's rock-cut site lies ~8 km from the town.
